title: Apples, Granny Smith, with skin, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Granny Smith apples are a green variety with a bright tart‑sweet flavor, covered by a thin edible skin. They are grown in temperate climates and are commonly eaten fresh or used in cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Granny Smith cultivar was developed in the United States in the mid‑19th century.
These apples retain their crispness even after extended storage.
Their tart flavor makes them popular for pies, salads, and sauces.
The skin is rich in antioxidants, so it is recommended to keep it on when eating.
Granny Smith apples are often used as a maturity indicator in scientific studies.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Apples provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, increases satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: Apples have a low energy density, making them a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Contain polyphenols
items.content: Polyphenolic compounds act as antioxidants and may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Support heart health
items.content: Potassium and soluble fiber contribute to normal blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Apple allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to apples, especially if they are sensitized to pollen.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: If the apples are not organic, wash them thoroughly to reduce pesticide intake.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of apples can cause gas due to fermentation of fiber in the gut.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Granny Smith apples can be eaten fresh, sliced into salads, used in baking, sauces, and smoothies. Keeping the skin on is recommended because it holds most of the nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store apples in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, in a perforated plastic bag. At room temperature they keep for up to a week, and in the fridge for up to a month.
